$comment: Pins the oidc-side half of `$defs/IdentityHint`'s if/then/else in `aitp-manifest.schema.json` (issue #59): `type: "oidc"` REQUIRES `issuer` and FORBIDS `public_key`. The `pinned_key`-requires-`public_key` half and the hint-level `type`/`subject` requirement are already exercised incidentally by every success fixture's `identity_hint`; only the oidc-forbids-`public_key` branch had no vector anywhere in the pack — id-008 pins the same rule at the handshake's identity DESCRIPTOR (RFC-AITP-0002 §1, a different object, exchanged in MUTUAL_HELLO with a live JWT proof), not the Manifest's static identity_hint. Otherwise byte-identical to man-001's non-expired, well-formed Manifest body, so the added `public_key` is the only defect under test.
description: Manifest `identity_hint` has `type: "oidc"` and also carries `public_key`. RFC-AITP-0003 §3.1 requires the oidc branch of `identity_hint` to omit `public_key`: the agent's public key is already encoded in the Manifest's own `aid`, so a second copy in the hint creates an ambiguity over which key is authoritative — the same rationale RFC-AITP-0002 §1 states for the handshake's identity descriptor. `aitp-manifest.schema.json`'s `$defs/IdentityHint` enforces this structurally (`then.not.required: [public_key]` under the oidc branch). Receivers MUST reject with MANIFEST_INVALID.

expected.rationale: `public_key` is forbidden on the `oidc` branch of `identity_hint` (RFC-AITP-0003 §3.1; `aitp-manifest.schema.json`'s `$defs/IdentityHint` encodes this as `then.not.required: [public_key]`). The Manifest is otherwise well-formed and unexpired, so the forbidden member is the only defect. This is a structural (schema) rejection of the Manifest body, which the registry maps to MANIFEST_INVALID.
